stem:
Heena compares two planet cards: Planet P is nearer the Sun with a thin atmosphere; Planet Q is farther out but has a thick heat-trapping atmosphere. One card looks reddish and one looks bluish.

Which statement is the best scientific judgment?

options.text: Planet P must be hotter than Planet Q solely because it is closer; atmosphere never needs checking.
Greater distance generally means less solar energy and a colder trend, but Planet Q's thick atmosphere can trap heat and change that simple distance rule.
With similar atmospheres ignored, the farther planet is generally the hotter one.
A reddish planet is always hotter than a bluish one, so colour decides temperature.

teacher.key_rationale: Distance sets a general temperature trend, but a thick atmosphere can trap heat and change it.
